title: Social Problems
description: Name what breaks the peace and what keeps it (a fight, a conflict, an insult, hostility, hooliganism, anger, to yell, to threaten, to hurt, to apologize, tolerance, flexibility, fair play, a compromise); sort English nouns into countable and uncountable and read what follows from that choice — a and one only in front of a countable singular, many, few and a number of in front of a countable plural, much and an amount of in front of an uncountable, a singular verb after it whatever its meaning, and a partitive (a piece of, an item of, a slice of) when you really must count it, with the traps that cost marks every year (information, advice, news, furniture, homework, work, progress, money, traffic, damage, violence); read a table of figures and draw only the conclusion they support; compare with the comparative between two and the superlative among three or more, built with -er / -est on short adjectives, more / most on long ones and the irregular pairs good-better-the best, bad-worse-the worst, little-less-the least, much and many-more-the most, far-farther or further-the farthest or the furthest; and say who obliges, who permits and who arranges with the causative verbs make, let and have followed by a bare infinitive — all through the vocabulary of child labour (to estimate, labour, manufacturing, to endure, deprivation, to hinder, survival, to contribute, access, to drop out, trade) and of children who grow up without their parents (siblings, consent, a foster home, to come to a head)
